commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 certify (PR #1300): diff changes the Brazil gate in every generated composition from `not entry_is_line_b` to `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum` and re-grounds the steel parameter proof from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02; report says "The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage".
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had.

triage.verifier_justification: The diff changes encoded meaning in two rule formulas (`ieepa_component_rate`, `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions`): the Brazil IEEPA carve-out stops being gated on `entry_is_line_b` — the witness harness's identity flag for HTS 7601.10.30.00, which this very module elsewhere uses as `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_b` — and is re-grounded on the membership input `entry_is_section_232_aluminum`. The source is class-based, not line-based: 9903.01.77 reads "Except for products described in headings 9903.01.78-9903.01.83 and 9903.01.90, articles the product of Brazil...", 9903.01.83 covers "articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum ... of Brazil", and 9903.85.02 (which the module's own unchanged proof atom already quotes) is the note-19(g) aluminum class, so the old per-line predicate had no basis in the cited text and was inoperative in a chapter-26 (ores/slag/ash) composition. That is a condition with no source basis that the fix re-grounds — untraceable_branch, not merely added scope, since the module's own summary already declared these as membership-semantic caller inputs. The remaining half of the diff (steel proof atoms 9903.81.87/.88 → 9903.82.02, same "+ 50%" excerpt, versions untouched) is mechanical provenance and does not carry the classification.

triage.verifier_notes: Refutation attempts that failed: (a) "it's a generated-surface generalization, not a correction" — the PR does frame stage 2 as decoupling from witness exemplar flags and claims witness-slice equivalence, but the witness slice contains no chapter-26 line, so for this module the old gate could never fire and never implemented 9903.01.77's exclusion; (b) "mechanical" — the proof-atom re-grounding is mechanical, but two formula lines changed truth conditions, so the module change is substantive; (c) "wrong_entity_or_scope" is the strongest alternate kind (exclusion applied to one line instead of the 232-aluminum population); I rejected it because the discarded predicate is a test-fixture identity flag with no counterpart in the cited text at all, which is exactly what untraceable_branch names ("re-grounds"). Verified source text through the pinned release (corpus us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap): 9903.01.77, 9903.01.81/.82/.83/.90, 9903.85.02, 9903.82.02 all resolve; us/statute/hts/9903.81.87 does NOT resolve in this vintage, which corroborates the report's "stale locator" note for the steel proof change. Two residual issues for a reviewer, neither changing this verdict: (1) the post-fix gate excludes only 232 aluminum, while 9903.01.77's exclusion set (9903.01.78-.83 and .90) also covers steel, wood, vehicles, semiconductors, copper and civil aircraft — a residual unrepresented_clause in the encoding after this fix; (2) the exclusion proof atom cites us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219, which in the resolver's corpus vintage returns a page of derivative-article HTS numbers, not the quoted exclusion sentence — the page locator looks vintage-stale even though the substance is confirmed via 9903.01.77/.83 and 9903.85.02.
